subject: Pricing and commitment options — Follow-up & startup discount request
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Connor Jordan <connor.jordan@fasthealth.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: pricing & commitment options (post-call recap)

Connor — thanks for taking time today. Quick recap and clear next steps so we can get a formal quote over to your procurement team.

Call recap:
- Primary use: patient triage + summary generation for virtual care; inference-heavy prompts with long context windows.
- Rough volume: you estimated 40M–60M tokens/month initially, with a growth profile to ~100M tokens/mo in 9–12 months.
- Budget signal: you mentioned $20k–$30k/month as a comfortable range for Yr1.
- Key constraints: Series A startup with CFO oversight; needs a predictable unit cost and a procurement-friendly contract (SOW/PO).

Pricing & unit-economics discussion items (from call):
- Baseline (hosted, on-demand): roughly $1,200 / 1M tokens for the unoptimized model we discussed.
- Engineering levers: quantized model + batching/KV cache can materially reduce unit cost — realistic target we discussed: $350–$800 / 1M tokens depending on reserved capacity and model variant.
- Your target: you said you wanted to get to roughly <$1,000 / 1M tokens; noted as a negotiation target.

What I need from you to proceed with a formal proposal:
1) Confirm whether FastHealth is eligible for our startup program (Series A is typically eligible) — any grant/accelerator notes to include?
2) Confirm a commitment preference: a) 12-month committed-use (preferred) or b) 24-month for deeper discounts, and an initial ramp profile (months 1–3 expected tokens).
3) Who should receive the official quote/PO (name/email at procurement)?

Attachments included: Redwood-Startup-Tiers.pdf (startup benefits & tiers), Draft-MAP-2yr.xlsx (illustrative committed-use math).

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm eligibility and procurement contact.
- Me: put together 2 pricing options (startup + 12m commit; committed reserved 24m) and a one-page impact table for CFO.
- Optional: 30-min follow-up with Dev (our infra SE) to validate ramp assumptions.

Thanks — I’ll draft the quote once you confirm the procurement contact.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

- Confirming FastHealth is Series A (post-seed), ~40 engineers, ~35 people in product/clinical. We should qualify for startup discounts.
- Our best estimate after the call: baseline 45M tokens/mo in Q1 of the contract, ramping to 80–90M by month 9.
- Budget: our leadership is comfortable with ~$25k/month net cash outlay in year 1. Anything north of $35k/mo will be a stretch without a stronger discount or committed pricing.

Procurement contact for formal quote / PO is:
Dana Lee <dana.lee@fasthealth.com> (Head of Finance, FastHealth) — please include procurement@fasthealth.com on the formal quote.

A couple asks for the proposal:
1) Can you send an option that includes a startup credit or upfront support credit for year 1?
2) We would like a clear per-1M token price (input+output) and the expected monthly cost at the 45M and 90M volume bands.
3) Any SLA or account management add-ons that affect price should be flagged separately.

I’ll loop in Dana if you want a quick procurement sync.

—Connor

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: pricing levers to include in the FH proposal

Internal notes (not for external):
Marissa asked for concrete options to hit their ~$25k/mo budget given 45M ramp. Thinking through levers: 
1) Startup program: 20% off list for first 12 months + $10k platform credit (we can modestly push credit if approved by sales leadership).
2) Committed-use reserved pools: for inference, a 12-month reserved commit (monthly flat fee with usable token allowance) gets ~35% off list. 24-month can push to ~50% off list depending on the commit size and model quantization.
3) Model variant optimization: propose a quantized-v2 of the selected model as default for production — budget impact: ~2.0–2.5x cheaper than unoptimized host. We should itemize both 'unoptimized' and 'optimized' per-1M prices.

Proposed two-option structure to present to Dana: 
- Option A (Startup + 12m commit): startup tier (20% off) + 12m committed use sized for 45M avg first 3 months, then ramp. Net effective price target: ~$600 / 1M tokens (input+output) — includes reserved discount + quantized runtime assumption. Expected monthly spend at 45M: ~$27k (close to their budget if we include a $5k startup credit).
- Option B (24m committed + volume scaling): deeper commit to reach their 9–12m growth; net effective price target: ~$420 / 1M tokens. With a 24m MAP and a modest up-front commit credit, expected monthly spend at 45M: ~$19k; at 90M: ~$38k.

Operational asks: need Sales Ops to finalize MAP math and DocuSign-ready contract. If we want to be aggressive, confirm ability to offer an extra 5% off on top of Option A if they sign within 30 days.

Alex
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Connor Jordan <connor.jordan@fasthealth.com>, Dana Lee <dana.lee@fasthealth.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Finance Procurement <procurement@fasthealth.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal options and next steps (startup + committed discounts)

Connor / Dana — following up with two formal option outlines based on our conversation and internal pricing levers. I attached the Draft-MAP-2yr.xlsx for detailed math and the Startup tiers doc. Below are the one-page summaries we discussed.

Option A — Startup + 12-month committed use (recommended initial path)
- Eligibility: FastHealth qualifies for Redwood Startup Tier (Series A).
- Incentives: 20% startup discount on list for first 12 months + $5,000 platform credit toward usage (one-time).
- Commitment: 12-month MAP sized at expected Q1 run-rate (45M tokens/mo initially).
- Effective unit price (input+output, quantized runtime): ~$600 / 1M tokens.
- Estimated monthly cost at 45M tokens: ~$27,000 (net of credit).
- Quick-close incentive: additional 5% off effective price if signed within 30 days.

Option B — 24-month committed use (deeper discount for growth)
- Incentives: longer MAP, larger reserved pool + standard volume tiers.
- Effective unit price (input+output, quantized runtime): ~$420 / 1M tokens.
- Estimated monthly cost at 45M tokens: ~$18,900; at 90M tokens: ~$37,800.
- Notes: requires heavier upfront commitment; better unit economics over time.

Additional notes:
- Baseline on-demand (no commit) for the discussed model is ~ $1,200 / 1M tokens (unoptimized). We show both baselines and optimized projections in the attached spreadsheet.
- SLA & AM: Standard enterprise SLA included with committed plans; AM/onsite support is add-on (line-item in MAP).
- Procurement: Draft-MAP-2yr.xlsx is attached for Dana. If you confirm Option A or B, we will send a DocuSign-ready MAP. HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567. DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/en/document/abc123

Ask: please confirm preferred option (A or B), and whether we should build the MAP to start at 45M tokens/mo or include a 3-month ramp (recommended). Once you confirm, I’ll get Sales Ops and Legal to move to a formal MAP/DocuSign.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min procurement sync next week if useful.

Best,
